name: proxy-switch
desc: Free, open-source proxy switcher for Windows — toggle system proxy profiles with one hotkey, offline. 100 MB portable, no account, MIT.
features: ✅ **Profile list** — save named HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS and PAC configurations and switch with one click
✅ **Global hotkey cycle** — Ctrl+Alt+P rotates through profiles without opening a window
✅ **Per-network memory** — remembers which profile belongs to office, home and lab Wi-Fi by SSID
✅ **Bypass list editor** — manage the no-proxy-for list per profile with comma-separated editing
✅ **Status truth** — tray icon reflects what WinINET actually uses, not what you think you set
✅ **Light and dark tray packs** — readable on both taskbar themes
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, portable, offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | Feature | **proxy-switch** | Proxy Switcher | ProxyCap | Windows Settings |
| Named profiles with hotkey | **Yes** | Partial | Yes | No |
| Bypass list editor | **Yes** | Partial | Yes | Clunky |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Installer | Installer | With OS |
faqQ: how to switch proxy settings quickly on Windows?
faqA: The Settings proxy page is four clicks deep with no profiles, and QA teams end up toggling fields by hand dozens of times a day. proxy-switch stores named profiles, cycles them from a hotkey and can bind a profile to a Wi-Fi network automatically. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline with no account.
s1: Dark profile list (#121417, blue #60A5FA): three profiles (Office SOCKS, QA HTTP, Direct) with radio dots, active one glowing, hotkey chip below.
s2: Profile editor: host and port fields, PAC URL input, bypass list text area, test connection button with latency readout.
s3: Auto-rules view: SSID to profile mapping table, tray theme preview pair, log of last ten switches with timestamps.
